method: Intersect the six frozen per-source screens with current hold-editorial decisions. A closure-ready lower bound requires an earlier high-confidence unsuitable/nonreusable classification, an explicit bespoke/source-specific/transparent/compositional/literal/ordinary or no-stable-unit reason, and no unresolved-language/owner/naturalness cue in the source-specific rationale. All others remain open. This is conservative documentary triage, not automatic rejection.
sopBasis: P70–P74 require exact source, complete linguistic unit, catalogue comparison and verified/hold/rejected status with concrete reason.
P79 permits idioms, phrasal verbs, figurative uses and natural reusable collocations; absence of idiomaticity alone is not grounds to reject a natural collocation.
P85/P90/P97 require seven distinct learner decisions; a transparent or one-off sentence without a distinct transferable decision is not a course unit.
P290/P350 require unsuitable/duplicate items to be held or rejected before audio while preserving evidence.

recommendedWorkflow: For each closure-ready row, retain exact source/provenance and record a concrete rejection reason such as one-off imagery, transparent statement with no distinct learner decision, or literal context; do not create a lesson or audio. An editor must accept the disposition before changing its action.

For open rows, use the stated blocker: grammar/naturalness/source sense check, prior-owner comparison and bounded detector, or a seven-decision pilot. Do not close an item merely because its source is not a fixed idiom; P79 also allows natural reusable collocations.
Keep any rejected source traceable and separate from live selected lessons. A future strong reference or approved lesson can reopen the decision.
